Unconventional: Yes

Comments: On location to witness the conclusion of 72 hr. Pressure Build Up Tests (PBUTs) being performed on all (5) wells on the Hunter pad., the Hunter 21HC, 22HC, 23HC, 5H and 6H. These PBUTs are being performed to assess the recent remedial work, CET (Casing Expansion Tool), deployment performed on all (5) Hunter wells production casing strings. This is the 3rd post CET deployment PBUTs being performed on these wells. - All (5) wells on the pad are in production. The (20x13) annuli are capped and set up to vent to atmosphere via Sentry valves. The (13x9) and the (9x5) annuli are set up to vent to a production tank via 2" common vent line. All annuli were closed when I arrived. - Upon arrival I met with CALLC Field Reps. Andrew Sivle and Victor Kanuik and Creston Consultant Reps., Shane Reimold and William Dolan. Starting at approx. 08:30 ending annuli pressures were checked using a digital Crystal gauge. Gas checks were performed by Creston Reps., using a Bascom Turner Gas Explorer meter. Creston Consultants collected gas samples off annuli, where present, and will send out for isotopic analysis. - Ending pressures, gas checks and time of gas sample collections are listed below for all the HUNTER Pad wells. - HUNTER 5H: (20x13): 0.0 psi.; 0% CH4; No sample collected (13x9): 19 psi.; 59% CH4; Sample collected @ 08:40 (9x5): 413 psi.; 68% CH4; Sample collected at 08:45 - HUNTER 6H: (20x13): 0.0 psi.; 23,500 ppm spike,drop off to 0%) CH4; No sample collected (13x9): 0 psi.; 96% CH4; Sample collected @ 08:55 (9x5): 565 psi.; 82% CH4; Sample collected @ 09:05 - HUNTER 22HC: (20x13): 0.0 psi.; 59% CH4; Sample collected @ 09:10 (13x9): 0.0 psi.; 44% CH4; Sample collected @ 09:20 (9x5): 149 psi.; 84% CH4; Sample collected @ 09:25 - HUNTER 21HC: (20x13): 4 psi.; 44% CH4; Sampled collected @ 09:30 (13x9): 44 psi.; 79% CH4; Sample collected @ 09:40 (9x5): 57 psi.; 85% CH4; Sample collected @ 09:45 - HUNTER 23HC: (20x13): 0.0 psi.; 0% CH4; No sample collected (13x9): 15 psi.; 89% CH4; Sample collected @ 09:55 (9x5): 54 psi.; 87% CH4; Sample collected @ 10:05 - All (5) wells (20x13) annuli were returned to open and venting to atmosphere via Sentry valves and the (13x9) and (9x5) annuli were opened and venting to production tank @ 10:05.

Comments: On 4/11/2024, DEP representative John Rogers conducted a drilling/completions inspection at the Seneca Resource's Taft 851 well site located in Middlebury Township, Tioga County. It was 56 degrees, overcast and lightly raining when I arrived on location. When I arrived at the site, I met Seneca's Company man, Justin Green and HSE coordinator, Wayne Fletcher. Justin described current operations as follows: The Patterson 801 drilling rig is set up on site drilling production on four of five new wells. This rig arrived on site and started drilling on 3/31/2024. They were currently drilling the production section on the 76HU well and were in the process of drilling the curve, currently being at 11,228 feet. The lateral section will follow with the total depth expected to be 25,544 feet. Justin accompanied me on the site inspection. The rig and ancillary equipment were stationed on secondary containment. Chemicals were staged on secondary containment. There were 10 frac tanks on the northeast side of the rig staged in secondary containment, these being used for various drilling fluids. There were two frac tanks on the southeast side of the rig that were used to store rainwater collected from the pad surface. This water was being used for drilling fluids. The drill cuttings were being solidified with a plant-based substance called slate dry and with wood pellets prior to being transported offsite to a waste disposal facility. I did witness drill cuttings being piled up above the level of the exterior wall of an open top tank. I discussed keeping the level of the material low enough to allow for necessary free board.Due to recent rainfall, water puddles were present on the pad surface. I sampled a channel of water along the east side of the north perimeter berm that had demonstrated in prior inspections as having elevated levels of conductivity. The water field tested at 2.36 mS conductance near where a white residue could be seen on the gravel. The water field tested at 2.13 near the pad outfall in the center of the north perimeter berm and field tested at 2.11 mS as the water was running down the outfall. The water was flowing down to the northeast end of the sediment basin. The flow of water leading into the sediment basin field tested at 2.15mS conductance. Water leaving the sediment basin field tested at 0.869 mS conductance. Water flowing off location field tested at 0.88 mS conductance.No E and S issues were observed during the time of the inspection. Temporary compost filter socks have been installed throughout the construction site. I did witness emerging vegetation in the constructed areas but the requirements for permanent stabilization have not been met yet. Three sediment traps and one sediment basin have been installed on site and along the access road. They have not been converted to PCSM BMPs yet. Standing water was present in the basins.Violations are still outstanding for inspection ID 3724668 and ID 3736567 for a 6' x 60' puddle of water with elevated conductance and with a white substance in it; discovered on the unprotected pad surface and flowing into the sediment basin during drilling operations. The DEP recommends the following: 1. Continues the process of determining the source of contamination as witnessed in this and prior inspections. 2. Assess the area of elevated conductance fluid on the north side of the pad and entering the sediment basin. Clean and report as necessary.3. Maintain adequate levels of freeboard in open-topped containers including the half-round dumpsters being used for drill cuttings.4. Continue to monitor the stability and functionality of the sediment traps and sediment basin and repair as necessary.I left the site at 1300 hours.

Comments: Routine field inspection performed in late morning with cold, partly sunny weather conditions, and 29 degrees. Last inspection performed on 1/3/19, more than 3 years ago. Wellhead is located in partially wooded area along cleared access pathway ~175' SE of surface/ground production equipment (photo #1). The wellhead is in close and visible proximity to the production facility (photo #2). At the wellhead surface casing valve is open, closed valves to ports upper and lower, upper port valve open with plumbed copper tubings and open valve to right side plumbed rubber hose to stick up tubular plumbed to sales/production; annulus is buried, unable to determine if vented (photo #3). No Well label/marker is affixed to wellhead. The wellhead is in close, visible proximity to the production facility and does require a well label/marker (photo #2). Some trace to occasionally moderate corrosion at the wellhead on the production/surface casing steel unions, lubricator, and tubulars. The surface/ground production facility, one 50 bbl poly tank, and one 100 bbl steel tank all contained by a shallow earthen dike (photo #4). Valve closed on main tubular feeding separator and closed valves to and from separator (photo #5). A 31-day production chart is present, with no markings dated 12/1/22 (photo #6). No production is being recorded. Well posting signage affixed to steel tank with all information about well and current Operator present, except the Operator contact address information (photo #7). Fair to occasionally moderate corrosion on ground production unit equipment and steel tank. Notice of violation (NOV) issued for Well posting OGA3211(G). The Department is requesting Operator add contact address information to the permanent well posting signage affixed at the surface production facility. The Operator has not submitted 2021 Mechanical Integrity Assessment (MIA) for this well. No MIA submitted by the Operator for 2021, 2020, and 2019. The last MIA value officially submitted was back in 2018 stating 0 psig. Notice of violation (NOV) issued for Operating Wells - Mechanical Integrity reporting 78.88(e). The Operator submitted annual production reported (APR) in 2021 of 0 Mcf recorded over 365 days. The 2021 annual production report submitted indicates that this well was not in production during the 2021 production year. Additionally, this well was noted as having 0 or blank production values under the gas and/or oil quantity columns and noted as Well Temporarily Not Producing under the non production comments columns of the 2021, 2020, and 2019 production reports. The last reported production value was in 2018 of 332 Mcf recorded over 214 days. This well is shut in with no recorded production at the surface/ground production facility and continues to be temporarily not producing.

Violation ID: 956914
Permit API: 083-56364
Unconventional: No
County: McKean
Municipality: Lafayette Twp
Inspection Type: Routine/Complete Inspection
Inspection Date: 5/25/2022
Comments: This well was stimulated on 5/17/2022 and is currently being produced with a pump jack. The operator information is displayed on the pump jack. The pit used during the completion of this well has been reclaimed. Earth disturbance associated with reclaiming this pit and installing gathering lines alongside the spur road to the location has not been temporarily stabilized. A film of oil is evident on numerous trees along the southern edge of the location (beyond the pit). Stained soil with elevated specific conductivity (SPC) is also evident along various pathways across the forest floor downslope of where the pit was located. This is indicative that during the notching and/or frac'ing of this well, fluids associated with doing so were not sufficiently directed and/or contained in a pit. Two valves on the frac tank located at the southwestern corner of the well site are currently open and brine/production fluids are actively dripping out of them. Crude oil is pooled at both ends of the tank near the discharge points (valves) and the soil is stained for several feet downslope of each. SPC readings of the soil near the discharge points exceeded the upper limits of my field meter (20,000 uS/cm). Trees near the west side of the tank appear stressed as a result of the discharge from the tank. These observations are indicative that an appreciable (unknown) amount of brine/production fluids were released through the open valves on this tank. I contacted Justin Hansen of Bull Run and scheduled a field meeting to review these findings and discuss remediation options.

properties.summary: Environmental Health & Safety violation issued on 2019-06-26 to Minard Run Oil Co in Jenks Twp, Forest county. properties.content:
Report Details
Operator: Minard Run Oil Co
Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date: 2019-06-26
Violation Code: SWMA 610(1) - UNLAWFUL CONDUCT - Person dumped or deposited, or permitted the dumping or depositing, of solid waste onto the surface of the ground or underground or into the waters of the Commonwealth, without a permit for the dumping of such solid wastes from DEP.
Violation ID: 854470
Permit API: 053-27204
Unconventional: No
County: Forest
Municipality: Jenks Twp
Inspection Type: Incident- Response to Accident or Event
Inspection Date: 2019-06-26
Comments: Site of oil release reported on 6/21/2019 was on a tank battery located east off Salmon Road in a forested area. Oil was released from a hole in the bottom of one of the tanks located in a plastic lined secondary containment. An estimated several barrels of oil were released into the secondary containment. The valved discharge pipe through the secondary containment embankment was open for an unknown period of time after the tank was breached allowing the flow of an estimated one barrel of oil to be released to the ditch north of the tank battery. The oil released into the ditch flowed 10-15 feet in the ditch along the access road until it reached the culvert pipe under the access road, it then flowed through the culvert pipe under the road and continued to 300-400 feet through vegetation down grade from the tank battery. A backhoe was brought in at some point after the oil release and a ditch was dug approximately 70-80 feet down grade of the tank battery to contain the oil release. A second ditch was dug approximately 275 feet north and down grade of the first ditch to contain the oil flow already beyond the first ditch. Absorbent pads and loose absorbents were used to collect oil from the atop the water collected in the ditches. The second ditch/trap was set up with drains to allow water to siphon off leaving the oil in containment. Some oil residue was found on the vegetation east of the lower ditch in a connected depression and in the vegetation 10-20 feet north of the ditch/trap. There was no evidence of oil residue beyond these two areas. The oil and water remaining in the secondary containment was removed by a vacuum tanker truck via the discharge pipe, the remaining oil was removed from the leaking tank as well as from the the other tanks on site on Friday, June 21. There were several precipitation events after the oil was released to ground, one on Friday June 21st, the day of the event, another on Monday June 24, the runoff from these events carried the oil down grade to the above mentioned areas. You are hereby requested to follow Department Policy 550-5000-001, Addressing Spills and Releases at Oil &Gas Well Sites or Access Road. This Policy sets forth the procedures that should be followed to resolve the violations associated with the spill/discharge/release noted in this Notice of Violation by using either the Act 2 or the Alternative Remediation Process. A copy of the Policy is attached for your review.

properties.content:
Report Details
Inspection Client: EQT ARO LLC
Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety

Violation Code: 78a56(a) - TEMPORARY STORAGE - Operator failed to contain regulated substances and wastes used at or generated at a well site in a tank, series of tanks or other storage structures approved by the Department.
Violation ID: 8159689
Permit API: 081-21879
Unconventional: Yes
County: Lycoming
Municipality: McIntyre Township
Inspection Type: Incident- Response to Accident or Event
Inspection Date: 9/19/2023
Comments: This inspection was conducted in response to a notification from the operator that on 9/18/23 a leak was discovered in a GPU on Pad A which led to the release of an unknown quantity of produced fluid to the pad surface. I met with EQT representative Zac Subra upon arriving on Pad A. He showed me where the produced fluid leak occurred inside of GPU #3. He also showed me where the fluid overflowed the interior containment of the GPU and flowed outside of the GPU and onto the pad surface to the southwest of the GPU. A Waste Management crew was excavating the impacted area of the pad during this inspection. Mr. Subra said that the fluid appears to have traveled a couple of inches into the pad surface and then moved toward the southwest pad edge under the surface. A sump present in the stormwater channel along the southwest side of the pad had fluid in it with an electrical conductivity (EC) of 700 uS/cm. Mr. Subra stated that the initial EC reading taken in this sump was approximately 700 uS/cm and later it increased to approximately 1700 uS/cm. A smaller puddle of fluid approximately 25 feet to the north in the channel had an EC of 760 uS/cm during this inspection. No other fluid was observed in the channel or on the pad surface. The Department recommends vacuuming out the fluid in the southwest stormwater channel.Mr. Subra said that they plan to pursue Act 2 remediation due to the unknown volume of the release. Environmental consultant Penn E and R was present during this inspection. Mr. Subra said that Penn E and R were performing electrical conductivity screening and would take samples for the Act 2 remediation. Violations noted against permit 081-21855 for the produced fluid release to the surface of Pad A.Violations remain outstanding for the produced fluid release to Pad B from 2/6/23.

Comments: On December 15, 2023, I conducted an inspection of the WL Hopkins Well Site. The inspection was conducted in response to a request made by an PA DEP OGI during an inspection conducted on 12/15/2023 (Sub-SAIR# 3660126). At the time of inspection, the following was observed:Act 9 Sign Installed, however the Operator of Record does not appear to be correct. The associated PPC plan and ER plan on site have not been updated to reflect the change in ownership. (Photo 11 and 12)The COASTAL Drill Rig was on site and connected to the well. The drill rig and associated equipment was not placed within secondary containment. (Photo 1)I observed fluid on the well pad surrounding the WL Hopkins 590312 Well and drill rig. I also observed fluid within the well cellar. I collected conductivity readings of the fluid on the well pad and within the cellar, which result in elevated conductivity readings. I also observed what appeared to be a light colored crystallin substance deposited on the well pad rock adjacent to the standing fluid. The crystallin substance appears to be salt which suggest that the fluid has been on site long enough to begin evaporation. The amount of fluid on the well pad appeared to be greater than 42 gallons. At the time of inspection, the Department was not previously notified by the Operator of a release of fluid to the well pad. (Photo 2 thru 10)While I was on site, I contacted Operator representative Kevin Wright (CONSOL/Leatherwood) to relay my observations related to the fluid release and recommend that the Operator being remediation immediately. Mr. Wright indicated that the Operator added brine to the well to kill the well on 11/15/2023.I am requesting clarification of the activity, date and time of when the fluid was added to the well bore and all information/inspections related to the monitoring of the well between 11/15/2023 and 12/15/2023. I am also requesting clarification of the source of the fluid added to the well bore on or around 11/15/2023.Violation are being issued for the release (78a.54, 78a57(a), 91.34(a), SWMA 301, 78a66(b)1,78a(b)1(i), 78a66(b)1(ii), 78a66(b)(2), 91.33(a) and 91.33(b).Violations are being issued for the failure to develop a site specific PPC plan and ER Plan. 78a55(a), 78a55(b), 78a55(c). 78a55(h).Violations are being issued for the failure to properly update the Act 9 Sign (78a55(i)(4)(D)(III).Violations are being issued for the failure to install secondary containment. (78a64(a))

Comments: On April 25, 2024 the Department conducted an inspection of the Augustine George 11039 access road located in Cecil Township, Washington County in regards to a complaint received on 04/24/24 CTS # 380091. The findings are as follows: At the time of the inspection, a truck was observed opening a valve and releasing what appeared to be freshwater onto the access road. Upon investigating this release, John Hulsey of Range Resources informed the Department that this fluid is freshwater and that the purpose of releasing said freshwater is to minimize the amount of dust caused from vehicles traveling up and down the access road. The released freshwater mixed with sediment as it flowed down the access road on to N Depaoli Road, traveled along the shoulder of N Depaoli and flowed off the shoulder into according to the site plans, an unnamed intermittent tributary to Millers Run. Conductivity readings were taken in the vegetation that is now impacted by sediment laden waters and they are as follows: 0.410 mS in the sediment laden puddle created from the flow going off the shoulder of the road, 0.464 mS in the vegetation adjacent to where the previous puddle reading was taken, 0.502 mS in some vegetation that is further in the intermittent tributary, and lastly 0.157 mS upslope of the Act 9 sign as a background reading. Though these readings subjugate that freshwater is being released, it is evident that sediment is still entering Waters of the Commonwealth. While onsite, the Department notified John Hulsey about the sediment entering the Waters of the Commonwealth and advised them to promptly cease all water release dust suppression activities on the access road.The Department recommends the Operator re-evaluate their dust suppression methods or implement measures to prevent sediment laden water from entering the intermittent unnamed tributary to Miller's Run.Based on today's inspection, violations shall be issued for the discharge of sediment into Waters of the Commonwealth.

Report Details

Violation ID: 907793
Permit API: 129-24892
Unconventional: No
County: Westmoreland
Municipality: Washington Twp
Inspection Type: Routine/Complete Inspection
Inspection Date: 2/08/2021
Comments: At the time of inspection, well appears to be equipped for production (Photo 1). Well label and tag present on well head (Photo 2). Pipe extending from brine tank appears to have a leak. The pipe appears to have significant rusting. The soil underneath the elbow joint of the pipe is saturated (Photos 3 and 4). Photo 5 show the underside of the pipe as it appears wet. The Department observed liquid dripping from the area shown. Two conductivity readings were taken from the saturated soil (Photos 6 and 7) showing readings of 6,410 microsiemens and 14,840 microsiemens. No background readings of the soil were recorded due to the ground being frozen everywhere excluding the affected area, however, due to the elevated readings of the affected area it appears that release is occurring. Photo 8 shows brine tank with well label present. Photo 9 shows the top of the brine tank lacking third-party protection. The Department recommends that the spill be remediated. The Department recommends the pipe be remediated or replaced. The Department recommends that the brine tank is protected against third-party acts. The Department requests inspection logs for the brine tank for the past 3 months. The Department requests information on how much fluid was lost and how the operator quantifies that information. The Department requests the waste manifest once it is available. The Department contacted both Lisa Raffle and Josh Martz of Diversified and notified them of the leak; they said someone would be out to remediate as soon as possible.

Permit API: 033-25118

Inspection Date: 9/14/2023
Comments: The Department received a complaint on 9/11/23 regarding a potential brine leak on the ground at conventional well 033-25118. I conducted a site inspection on 9/14/23. I observed a bare spot of soil inundated with deer hoof prints near the valve on the brine tank. An area of dead and/or stressed vegetation was also observed. In addition, some standing puddles were observed near the brine tank and in a ditch approximately 20' away from the brine tank. I screened the puddles using an Oakton meter for conductivity. Readings ranged from 16.93 mS/cm to 4.23 mS/cm. A grab sample was collected (3442-696) from one of the puddles near the brine tank and was sent to the Departments lab in Harrisburg to be tested for SAC 942 plus aluminum, bromide, and lithium. Based off screenings and dead vegetation the impacted area is at 20' x20'. After leaving the site I contacted Heather Empfield and Mark McCracken of Diversified and reported my findings. The Department recommends that operator investigates the brine release and based off the amount of brine released, the operator addresses the remediation in accordance with small spill policy 800-5000-001 or Act 2.Violations have been citied.

Permit API: 053-28071
Unconventional: No

Inspection Date: 9/25/2024
Comments: This conventional well is equipped for production with a pump jack. A sign containing the API number, well name, and operator information was posted on a stake near the well. The GPS coordinate on file for this well was verified as part of this inspection. Upon arrival to the site, it was evident that crude oil had recently leaked from a faulty stuffing box on this well. The discharged crude oil migrated onto the well site, then traveled linearly approximately 450 feet downslope of the well on the access road. The crude oil remained contained on the road surface and ultimately accumulated in a puddle of standing water at the bottom of the hill (see Photo 2). It is estimated that less than 1 barrel of crude oil has been released as part of this incident. No waterways have been affected from the event.A representative from Bull Run Resources, JR McLaughlin, was contacted in response to the event. He arrived to the site immediately to address the noted concerns. The leaking stuffing box was repaired and diapers were used to absorb the crude oil from the road surface and around the well head. Given there is no ongoing discharge and a bulk of the released product has been remediated, the violations associated with this incident are considered corrected.A future inspection will be conducted to ensure that the initial remediation efforts were sufficient.

Code Chapter 102, during and after earthmoving or soil disturbing activities, including the activities related to siting, drilling, completing, producing, servicing and plugging, constructing, utilizing and restoring the site and access road.
Violation ID: 8275383
Permit API: 129-24171
Unconventional: No
County: Westmoreland
Municipality: Allegheny Township
Inspection Type: Follow-up Inspection
Inspection Date: 5/18/2026
Comments: On May 18, 2026, the Department conducted a Follow Up Inspection of Oil and Gas Mgmt's Armstrong 2 gas well site direct access road following IR 4186406, where violations were continued for an inadequately stabilized shared and direct access road.Accompanying during today's inspection is DEP Environmental Trainee, Rosie Wise. A NOV response has yet to be received from the operator of this gas well following IR 3891447 when violations were issued for an inadequately stabilized shared and direct access road. However, the DEP has been in communication with the other operator who utilizes the shared portion of the access road and has begun working on repairing the shared access road. At the time of this inspection, the Department observed ongoing repairs to the shared access road, permanent stabilization of the shared access road has not been reached at the time of this inspection. Silt-fencing was observed to be installed on the side of the access road closest to the stream, and culverts and berms appear to be installed to direct water off of/away from the access road. (Refer to IR 4186406, for the closure of violations associated with sediment entering the Waters of the Commonwealth). At the time of this inspection, it appears that conditions of the direct portion of the access road leading to the Armstrong 2 gas well site are unchanged from IR 3891447, rutting and large pooling of stormwater were observed throughout the access road and an area of erosion as exposed a line from underground. No fluid leaks or fluid discharges were observed to be coming from the exposed surface of this line at the time of this inspection. Based on today's inspection, site observations of the direct portion of the access road being unchanged, and the shared portion not yet being permanently stabilized, violations issued for an inadequately stabilized shared and direct access road are to remain outstanding at this time.Violations associated with the Department's observations of the gas well site are assessed in IR 4203643.
